title: Aarhus, the Pa Pa Bue Viking Jazz Band and changing its style
summary: He plays first in Aarhus, with Fessor's Big City Band, then joins Pa Pa Bue's band for nearly a year and gets them playing his melodic swing way.

bands.name: Pa Pa Bue's Viking Jazz Band

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I'd also like to talk about my activities in Denmark. When I first did--- you know, I did the long tour---
Of course, the minute I hit Copenhagen, they sent me to Aarhus----- - my first job was in (inaudible)--
They must have ten good jazz bands in that town but I played my first four or five days in Denmark there and uh, and back

and forth -- I was constantly coming back and playing either radio shows or youth centers or colleges with different groups, but there's three or four groups in Denmark-- it started when I first went there five years ago, there was just one professional band and they're known all over England, Germany, Switzerland, Holland -- they play in that vicinity - all the time. And, it's called the Pa Pa Bue Band -- it's almost world famous--- not for their records; they've gone around; I've heard one of their records long before I went to Europe and I heard it here in America and it's really a fine jazz band---
It's Pa Pa Bue's Viking Jazz Band - right?

Yeah - but, there they just call them Pa Pa Bue. Jazz Band but it's actually the Viking Jazz Band and, uh, when they heard me play - the first few jobs that I had with a sizable band was with the Fessor's Big City Band and that was a swing band; I liked that very much -- they had some marvelous players. And, I was very surprised at the type of swing that they were playing. Wow -- it was really good. And, uh, so Pa Pa Bue heard me play with that band and he was losing a trumpet player -- now, I don't really--- I didn't want to join a band because I do better on my own - just travelling around but he asked me if I'd please join the band -- I joined him on New Year's Eve, about the second year I was in -- the beginning

of the second year I was over there and I did almost a year with him and I really changed the style of the band. They were playing sort of a little swing and Dixie Land and sort of a George Lewis---kind of thing; they were sort of mixed up, about what they really wanted to play. So, I got them going on---

--the way I play because after all, I was playing the melody in the band and they liked the idea. So, at least, I left these guys playing like the old Condon days; they still play that way. They like that way.
